cards.text: Grab an apron, friend! A new section of Proverbs opens with a heading: "The proverbs of Solomon:" That's Solomon, son of David, king of Israel (Proverbs 1:1), and his sayings come two lines at a time, often setting two kinds of people side by side.

cards.question: Solomon's very first proverb: "A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son grief to his mother." What's the big point?

answers.text: A son's choices affect his parents
A son's choices only affect himself
Parents decide how a son turns out

cards.text: Then Solomon talks money: "Ill-gotten treasures profit nothing…" That's worth less than the dead batteries I shared my old junk drawer with, and at least THEY swore they had a little charge left!

cards.question: Solomon says, "Ill-gotten treasures profit nothing…" So what does he say brings deliverance from death?
True or false: Solomon says the LORD lets the righteous go hungry.

cards.text: Next, Solomon holds up two pairs of hands: "Idle hands make one poor, but diligent hands bring wealth." I pack cookie boxes with a MUSTACHE, friend, and even I know which pair I'd hire.

cards.question: Solomon says the son who gathers in summer is wise, but the son who sleeps during harvest is disgraceful. What's the lesson?

answers.text: Work while the work is ready
Rest whenever you feel worn out
Leave the harvest to hired hands

cards.text: Harvest is the ONE season you do not hit snooze, and I say that as a stamper who snoozed an oven timer once and smelled it for a week. Then Solomon says, "Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence."

cards.question: Solomon says, "The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot." True or false: this proverb is about how people remember you.

cards.text: Solomon says, "A wise heart will receive commandments, but foolish lips will come to ruin." That's the guy who talks all the way through the safety briefing and then asks where the exits are.

cards.question: Solomon says, "He who walks in integrity walks securely…" True or false: he says the one who perverts his ways will never be found out.

cards.text: Solomon says, "He who winks the eye causes grief, and foolish lips will come to ruin." That line about foolish lips again, and with eyebrows THIS big, I couldn't wink if I tried!
Then Solomon says, "The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence." That second half matches verse 6 word for word.
Then Solomon says, "Hatred stirs up dissension…" Hatred is one comment in the group chat, and suddenly forty people are typing.

cards.question: Solomon says, "Hatred stirs up dissension…" Love works the other way: it ___ all transgressions.

cards.text: Solomon says, "Wisdom is found on the lips of the discerning, but a rod is for the back of him who lacks judgment." Then he says the wise store up knowledge, the way I store up chocolate chips before the holiday rush, but the fool's mouth invites destruction.

cards.question: Look how often these proverbs bring up the mouth and the lips. Solomon keeps paying close attention to what people ___.
Solomon says, "The wealth of the rich man is his fortified city, but poverty is the ruin of the poor." True or false: the fortified city is a picture of money as protection.
Solomon says, "The labor of the righteous leads to life, but the gain of the wicked brings punishment." What is he comparing?

answers.text: Where each one's earnings take them

cards.text: Back at the counter, friend. Solomon says, "Whoever heeds instruction is on the path to life…"

cards.question: Solomon pictures heeding instruction as the path to life. True or false: he says the one who ignores reproof stays on that path too.

cards.text: Then Solomon says, "The one who conceals hatred has lying lips, and whoever spreads slander is a fool." That's the coworker who says "Love your idea!" and then trashes your idea all afternoon in the break room.

cards.question: Solomon says, "When words are many, sin is unavoidable…" So the wise person keeps his lips ___.

cards.text: Somebody needs to tape that one RIGHT over the reply-all button, friend. Then Solomon says, "The tongue of the righteous is choice silver…"

cards.question: Solomon calls the tongue of the righteous choice silver. What's that picture saying about their words?
Solomon says, "The lips of the righteous feed many…" What does he say fools die for lack of?
True or false: Solomon says the blessing of the LORD enriches, but sorrow comes along with it.

cards.text: Solomon says, "The fool delights in shameful conduct, but a man of understanding has wisdom." Picture a guy bragging that he ran every red light on the way here, like it's a trophy.

cards.question: Solomon says, "…the desire of the righteous will be granted." What does he say happens to what the wicked man dreads?
Then a whirlwind passes through. True or false: Solomon says the righteous get swept away along with the wicked.

cards.text: Then Solomon paints a picture that makes you squint: "Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes…"

cards.question: Vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes. Who does Solomon say is like that to those who send him?

cards.text: You hand the slacker one small job, he says "On it!", and that's the last you ever hear of it. Next, Solomon says, "The fear of the LORD prolongs life, but the years of the wicked will be cut short."

cards.question: Solomon says, "The hope of the righteous is joy…" But what the wicked are counting on will come to ___.

cards.text: Then Solomon gives the upright a safe place to run: "The way of the LORD is a refuge to the upright…"

cards.question: Solomon says the way of the LORD is a refuge to the upright. What does he say awaits those who do evil?

cards.text: Solomon says, "The righteous will never be shaken…" and that's more than I can say for my chef's hat every time the oven door slams. As for the wicked, they "will not inhabit the land."

cards.question: Solomon says, "The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but a perverse tongue will be cut out." True or false: in Solomon's proverbs, what a person says carries real consequences.

cards.text: Solomon says, "The lips of the righteous know what is fitting, but the mouth of the wicked is perverse." Mouths, lips and tongues ALL over this chapter, friend, and here I am with a giant mustache parked right over mine like a filter!
